How to Apply
The application process is completed online through the UA Graduate School Application. You can start an application immediately, even if you don’t yet have all the required materials, and complete it as you go. We urge you to apply as soon as possible! Early applicants have the highest chances of admission. If you have any trouble with the application process, do reach out to us!
Materials
We accept unofficial documentation to streamline the application process. Official copies will only be requested at enrollment. To apply, you should submit the following materials:
You do not need to secure the support of potential advisors before applying. In fact, in our program group assignments take place after admissions and enrollment (however, please make sure to include your preferences in your statement of purpose, as mentioned below). Nevertheless, if you are interested in working with a specific faculty member, feel free to contact them to introduce yourself if you’d like.
Currently, the GRE is not required for admission.
Statement of purpose: Talk about any previous research experience, your scientific interests, and goals for graduate education. Explain any portions of your experience that you think should be brought to our attention, or that enhances your profile as an applicant. Mention the names of 2-3 faculty members in our department whose research interests you. This should be no longer than two pages. Submit this in PDF format if possible.
Resume/CV: Check out our graduate FAQ page to learn more about what to include in your resume or CV. Submit this in PDF format if possible.
Contact information for three references who have agreed to provide a letter of reference on your behalf. The letters, which should be confidential, will be submitted by your letter writers directly: they will be contacted by email with instructions to upload their letters. Choose writers that know you well and can evaluate your chances of success in a graduate program. If you have any research or work experience, make sure to include your faculty research advisor or supervisor: we would appreciate their evaluation of your proficiency outside of the classroom.
Unofficial transcripts from any undergraduate and graduate institution at which you completed at least 15 credits of work. These can be unofficial copies released to you or downloaded from your school’s website. You may also submit scans as PDF.
For international students: English proficiency scores are typically required (e.g. TOEFL, IELTS, DuoLingo), with some exceptions (visit the UA Graduate School’s International Admissions page). Unofficial score reports are accepted here as well; just submit a copy of the score report you received.
Payment of an application fee: $65 for domestic applicants; $80 for international.
Deadlines
Applications are for fall admission only (starting in mid-August each year). Spring or summer admission is not available. We encourage you to submit applications as early as possible; applications completed by December 1 receive priority consideration. Early applicants have several advantages. First of all, as an early applicant you will compete for available slots in a smaller pool, so you stand a higher chance of receiving an early offer of admission. Furthermore, you can be considered for more internal fellowship opportunities.
That notwithstanding, we still encourage you to apply even after those dates. Later applications will still be considered for admission and support as long as positions are available.
Admissions Requirements
To be considered for the graduate program, you should be near completion or have completed at least a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry or in a closely related field. Students generally must have earned a B average (3.0 out of 4.0 or equivalent) during their undergraduate and prior graduate work to gain regular admittance. Transcripts from international students that earned a three-year BS degree will be evaluated internally for equivalence to a US four-year BS degree. In most cases, students in these situations may be best served by earning an MS degree prior to entering the Ph.D. program.
In special cases, if your GPA score does not meet the minimum requirement you may be admitted under a “Permission to Continue” clause (PTC). In that case, a condition will be imposed on the admission, typically requiring to maintain a 3.0 GPA or better in the first 12 credit of graduate work at UA.
If your first language is not English, and you do not hold a degree from a US institution, then you will be asked to submit an unofficial English proficiency test score (e.g. TOEFL, IELTS, DuoLingo, PTE); however, first check these exemptions for English-speaking countries and other circumstances. For the TOEFL test, we look for a minimum score of 79; for the IELTS test, a minimum score of 6.5; for the DuoLingo test, a minimum score of 105. If your score is lower than that, you may still be admitted through “conditional language admission”, in which case your will be enrolled in English as a second language (ESL) classes on our campus according to your level of language proficiency. Please note, however, that this may slow your progress toward graduation.
Financial Support
Admission to our Ph.D. program typically includes five years of financial support, initially provided in the form of a graduate teaching assistantship, a full tuition scholarship, and health insurance coverage as appropriate; later in the program your research advisor may be able to provide you a research assistantship, or you may be awarded an internal or external fellowship. In any case, a determination on financial support will be made at the time an offer is extended.
Students admitted to the MS program are typically not offered financial support (review the Cost of Attendence for the fee structure for graduate studies at UA, including our MS program). You can apply for internal and external support, and you would also be eligible to be considered for graduate teaching assistantships once you are enrolled in our program, but their availability to MS students changes semester to semester, and a determination would only be made after you have spent at least a semester in our program.
For more information about funding opportunities, visit our Financial Support page.
Additional Fellowships and Scholarships
Starting in December in the year before admission, this department’s Graduate Recruiting Committee will select outstanding applications to be submitted for consideration for several University-wide graduate fellowships. Only completed applications can be considered. It is therefore in your best interest to complete all parts of your application by early December in order to be considered for these opportunities.
Questions?
Questions about the application process may be directed to one of our graduate program representatives.
